pr.title: Pass a CI review job when project review run refuses a pull request with nothing to review, such as a draft held for a fix
pr.head: 5cf0c9c71ba12649af60f3fc36cf1030ba0c6eea

summary: Projector can review pull requests in GitHub Actions. Each review job runs project review run, which reads the pull request, starts an agent, and checks that the agent published a verdict. Before it starts anything, the command refuses a pull request it must not review: one whose head is in a fork, a draft, or a closed one. It also skips a head this model already reviewed.

Most of those refusals exited 1, so the job's check turned red even though nothing had gone wrong. The common case was a race. An author marks a pull request as a draft to push a fix, and the job that started for the previous head reads the pull request after that and refuses it.

This pull request makes every refusal pass the job. A new skip() helper prints the reason and returns 0. Under GitHub Actions it also prints a ::notice:: workflow command, so the job's summary page says why the job reviewed nothing. A real failure, such as an agent that publishes no verdict, still exits 1 and posts a failure comment.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Refusal: a reason refusal() returns for not reviewing a pull request, such as a draft or a fork's head.
  • Skip: a run that reviews nothing and passes, which every refusal now is.
  • Workflow command: a line such as ::notice title=…::message that GitHub Actions reads from a step's output and shows as an annotation.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html: One Projector review of this head, clean, with no finding threads. It lists one suggestion: rewrap a long line in the plan's § 2.1 step 6.

groups.title: Refusals pass the job
groups.kicker: How project review run turns a refusal into a passing exit
intro: run() reads the pull request, asks refusal() whether to review it, and then checks for an existing verdict by this model. Before, a refusal raised ReviewError, which the CLI turns into exit 1. A closed pull request never reached refusal(), because review.pull_request raised on it first.

Now run() reads the pull request with review.read_pull_request, which returns a closed one, and refusal() checks the state first. Each refusal, and the already-reviewed skip, returns through skip(). Every one of them returns before the run adds the reviewing label or reaches the failure-comment path, so a skipped run leaves nothing on the pull request.

files.note: The state check in refusal(), the new skip(), and the early returns in run().

checks.text: GitHub's REST API reports a merged pull request as state: closed with merged: true, so this reads merged to name it.
The message holds only the repository, the number, a SHA prefix, and a review URL, so it needs no % or newline escaping for the workflow command. Checked by reading every message passed to skip().
Both returns come before change_labels adds reviewing and before the failure comment. Checked by reading run() to its end, and test_a_refused_run_adds_no_label asserts it.

files.note: assert_skipped checks the exit code, exactly one notice, no agent started, and nothing posted or labeled, for each refusal.

groups.title: Documentation and plan
groups.kicker: What the docs and the review-in-ci plan now say a refusal does
intro: docs/cli.md and docs/review-in-ci.md describe the new behavior, and docs/cli.md now lists the command's exit codes. The review-in-ci plan, which is in progress, updates its § 2.1 step 6, an acceptance row, and a test description, and adds § 11 to record the decision.

checks.text: The exit codes docs/cli.md lists match the CLI. In a scratch repository, a non-numeric pull request exited 2, an unknown --agent exited 1, and a missing pull request exited 1.
This line runs to 105 columns where the lines around it wrap near 76; the review lists rewrapping it as a suggestion.
